design_condition: The building is placed orthogonally along the edge of the historic complex, preserving its balance while forming a transition toward the surrounding urban fabric and a sheltered outdoor space.

positive.statement: The calibrated imprint inserts the emerging volume precisely and respectfully into the existing context.
Freeing the ground-floor corner clearly identifies the entrance and creates a sequence of shared meeting spaces.
The external space between the new and historic buildings is enhanced by a fluid connection between outdoor areas.
The differentiated structural proposal coherently rethinks the industrial character through prefabrication and serial production.
The greenery creates a coherent hortus conclusus while balancing use requirements and environmental aspects.
The lightweight structure is efficient, quick to build, and causes limited repercussions on the surroundings.
The envelope and glass-to-opaque ratio appear optimal and suitable for the intended energy certification.
External and internal noise protection is carefully documented.

negative.statement: The structural masonry spine is excessively formal and restrictive for the internal spaces.
A green roof or more defined green concept for the galleries could have provided environmental benefits.
The ecological aspects of the materials are not explicitly addressed.
